Document24 screening cases and six cases per split across12 engineering inputs. Middle-stratum jitter is not IID golfer data or full-range uniform sampling. Six-case linearq10 averages the first two order statistics; policy-quantile differences differ from quantiles of paired differences.

Specify delay, rate-limited lag-state increments, velocity resistance and capacity clipping in their implemented order. Velocity resistance is not elastic stiffness and delivered torque is not purely open-loop. Fixed-time planar error, peak individual hand force, squared-torque integral and speed spread do not measure ball dispersion, injury, metabolism or tracking stability.

Selection uses training objectives with candidate-dependent ranges. Leave-one-case-out membership is a sensitivity check, not a population frontier confidence interval; no dynamics rerun.

Separate attempted, solved, admissible and event-defined denominators. Missing numerical outcomes are not fabricated physical failures. Match holdouts to deployment questions; distinguish average from conditional calibration and parameter identifiability from predictive identifiability.

Early restrain and late drive differ in onset and late command as well as early command, so their comparison cannot isolate the opposing interval. Match information and constraints without erasing induced state changes. Equal tuning budgets, model ranking reversals and bimodality do not establish optimization equality or causal mechanisms; reviews are context, not human validation.

Point, Plane and Moment Arm. Define moment about a point without requiring that point to be inertial; distinguish this definition from angular-momentum balance. Define in-plane transverse direction separately from the plane normal. Collinear force has exactly zero ideal moment, but may transfer power or produce translation. Replace the misleading reference-to-arrow-tip dashed segment with the force line and its perpendicular distance from the reference.

Reference and Observer. A pure couple is reference-independent; a small nonzero resultant needs a bounded shift and tolerance. Transport both moment and rigid-body point velocity to preserve power. Component rotation differs from a moving physical observer, whose force power changes. Retain distributed force–velocity pairings when one rigid twist is insufficient.

Jacobian Duality. Explicit time-dependent kinematics adds prescribed-motion velocity and power. A Jacobian transpose maps an applied force into its generalized-force contribution, without requiring equilibrium or frictionless contact. Generalized speeds need not be coordinate derivatives; preserve dual forces and coordinate units when changing variables.

Singularity Scope. Distinguish inverse velocity amplification from force transmission. The independent diagonal example gives reciprocal scalings and exposes the force nullspace at exact rank loss. No infinite physical force, independent force control or universal biological non-identifiability follows. Instantaneous rank limits are not global path-reachability results.

Inertial Response. Same-state acceleration change depends on inverse inertia and applicable constraints. A positive off-diagonal mass entry can yield a negative cross-acceleration. Diagonalizing the example's mass matrix preserves the reconstructed response. Constraint reactions must change consistently with command; raw entries are not invariant mechanical causes.

Two-Hand Controls. Separate exact point-force couples from free moments, midpoint common/differential decomposition from other references, and a physical reversal from co-rotation or relabeling. Separation scaling assumes forces held fixed; dynamically recomputed reactions can change that scaling.

Allocation Matching. The provider fixes club inertia times a same-state control-only angular-acceleration difference at8 N m. It does not match the whole wrench or trajectory. The blend parameter interpolates two independently normalized actuator controls, not direct-moment fractions. At the wrist-only endpoint, opposing contact-force moments compensate direct moments above8 N m.

Metrics and Optima. Hand-force RMS is across two control-only vector norms at one instant, not a time RMS or total contact load. The norm of a difference is not a difference of norms. Torque cost is an unweighted six-command norm. Recompute stored extrema, closure residuals and grid minimizers; distinguish this restricted blend scan from all admissible allocations and human optima.

Evidence and Mechanism. Remove unsupported empirical specificity and retain the review citation as context. A negative force projection and geometric identity do not establish persistence or performance under changed reactions. Connect geometry to state, constraints, inertia, objectives and measurement.

Point Speed Versus Body Energy. Replace the ambiguous positive-acceleration/negative-power claim with a rigid-body endpoint formula and a manufactured rod counterexample. The tip accelerates tangentially at 1 m/s² while the body's total kinetic-energy rate is -1 W; the translational loss exceeds its rotational gain. For a fixed-mass particle, increasing speed still requires positive net power. These are different system/quantity statements, not an exception to work-energy balance.

Physical and Coordinate Energy. Use center-of-mass translation plus tensor rotational energy; distinguish fixed-axis reduction, coordinate cross-terms and explicit moving-base terms. A physical segment's energy is defined after specifying body and observer; distributing cross-terms among generalized coordinates is a different convention. Do not add moving-grip rotational energy directly to COM translation. The manufactured coordinate-mixing test preserves 2.5 J while diagonal-only accounting misses 1 J.

Power-Conjugate Motion. Declare material-point velocity, matched wrench reference and observer. Separate a segment moment contribution from joint actuator power using relative angular velocity. Equal/opposite moments can supply a distal segment while the actuator absorbs net mechanical power. Include other force/moment channels before claiming net segment energy change; no muscle/metabolic inference follows.

Storage and Boundary. Correct the worked example: 15 J hand work minus 2 J aerodynamic work raises whole-club mechanical energy by 13 J. Releasing 8 J of internal strain raises K+V by 21 J, not total storage by 21 J. A linked shaft/head example explicitly assigns shaft K+V increase of 5 J and all aerodynamic loss to the head: shaft total change -3 J, interface work 18 J and head gain 16 J reconcile to the same 13 J total. These are synthetic assignments, not measured golf values.

Impulse and Constraints. State net external impulse, inertial observer and fixed angular-momentum reference conditions. Distinguish fixed-circle radial force from a force directed toward moving hands. Internal joint reaction power can cancel for the combined system while transferring energy between segments; acceleration-term splits are not automatically physical energy supplies.

Sequence and Evidence. Speed-peak order alone identifies neither segment energy loss nor its destination. Separate the pinned double-pendulum E1 comparison from the coupled uncertainty H4 result and its face/path tradeoff. Tinmark's published abstract concerns 45 skilled golfers' kinematics; Robertson/Winter's abstract concerns two walking subjects and a sagittal model; McPhee is a narrative review. None supplies a new human causal intervention here.

Counterfactual Interpretation. Match admissible state, controller memory, parameters and event rules. Finite refinement/uncertainty tests provide bounded support. Loss of a ranking does not uniquely identify preparation or parameters; numerical and event changes remain alternatives. Pin all upstream source links to the book's declared immutable revision.

Figure Semantics. Give both plotted quantities explicit dimensionless normalization. Label the bar example as translational energy at fixed speed and vary mass alone; do not claim it demonstrates rotational inertia. Only make_speed_energy changes in the shared generator; all other function ASTs are preserved.

Correct the Review Attribution. The 92-study systematic kinematics review is Bourgain et al. (2022), not McPhee's narrative review. Preserve both with distinct purposes and add the missing bibliography record. The human-study list is a selected register, not a systematic search performed by this project.

Bound the EMG Findings. Use Kao et al.'s canonical authorship (Jobe is a coauthor), selected four scapular muscles, and 15 competitive male participants without inventing electrode type from the abstract. Robinson et al. measured bilateral extensor carpi ulnaris, not all wrist muscles, in 15 subelite right-handed men. Nonsignificance does not establish irrelevance or equivalence; EMG is not force.

Separate Sensor and Model Quantities. Koike's calibrated strain-gauge handle reconstructs palm resultants under fixed-reference and negligible-handle-inertia assumptions. Choi/Park's single six-axis internal grip sensor supports inverse-dynamics estimates of separate hand and net joint loads. Their reported hand-torque ratio is model-derived; grip modification, fixed trial order, possible bypass, and foam/sponge balls limit interpretation.

Retain Study and Mechanical Boundaries. Zheng's observational skill comparisons do not justify copying a professional's technique or injury prevention. Han's force plates and computed ground-interaction moments support associations, not identified energy pathways. Betzler's bounded shaft comparison does not establish universal stiffness effects. Peak sequence, force magnitude, and activation timing are not interchangeable measurements of energy transfer.

Explain Repeated-Measure Uncertainty. Derive a balanced independent-participant random-intercept example with explicitly manufactured variances. Verify its mean variance from a full covariance matrix: 11/150 versus the false independent-swing estimate 2/150, design effect 5.5. The equivalent count 300/11 is neither independent people nor a degrees-of-freedom formula. More repeats reduce residual uncertainty but leave the between-person term at fixed participant count.

Distinguish Statistical Targets. Hierarchical estimation, prediction for unseen participants, prediction for a known participant's new session, and causal identification require different designs. Participant holdout is relevant to unseen-person generalization, not a universal requirement for every association estimate. Preprocessing/model selection must respect the split. Neither prediction nor a mixed model automatically supplies causal identification.

Scope the Validation Gap and Integrate Channels. Absence of a complete validation dataset is bounded to the evidence assembled in this project. Explain why ground/body/hand/shaft/EMG/launch observations need synchronized mechanical accounting and why not every narrower question needs every channel. Pressure does not replace a contact wrench; stationary ideal ground contact can exchange momentum without supplying work.

Make Disagreement Diagnostic Without Overdiagnosis. A persistent sign mismatch after frame/timing/uncertainty checks can refute the specified prediction. Matching mechanics does not validate anatomy. Motion/load disagreement admits multiple causes, rather than uniquely proving underconstraint or compensation. Frozen tests, explicit deviations, consent-compatible release, and synthetic-data labels keep the inference auditable.

Replace the Certainty Pyramid. Four equal-width panels distinguish observations, mechanical inference, anatomical inference, and prospective tests. More sensing can constrain explanations without uniquely identifying biology. Only make_human_evidence changes in the shared generator; existing asset names and chapter anchor remain stable.

Separate Fixed, Prescribed, and Dynamic Bases. A prescribed base can move. It needs an enforcing reaction after other inputs are declared. The same reaction can change acceleration while doing zero instantaneous work at zero base velocity. Assigned torques and a prescribed path are not inherently invalid if their residual reaction and power are accounted for.

Correct the Replay Inference. With identical distal equations, inputs and compatible initial state, prescribing the baseline base path reproduces the distal solution under uniqueness when the removed input enters only base equations. Persistence is a consistency property; it does not prove feedback unimportant. Distinguish instantaneous intervention, integrated response, fixed input history and recomputed feedback policy.

Distinguish Mass From Trajectory Authority. Bounded-load, finite-time mass limits are not arbitrary prescribed accelerating paths. Force capacity, stiffness and feedback gain are separate assumptions. A translating hub does not acquire whole-body anatomy by having finite mass.

Make Coordinate Dependence Concrete. A manufactured cart-pendulum fixture diagonalizes inertia in horizontal COM coordinates while retaining the cart force in the angular generalized load. Newton balances, kinetic energy, force covectors and power establish that coordinate simplification does not remove physical interaction.

Close the Declared Energy Boundary. Include enforcing power, conservative storage once, represented flexible kinetic energy, dissipation and numerical projection work. Internal passive constraint powers cancel under compatible relative motion. Distinguish grip power, projected moment, rotational power and work. Numerical convergence is not physical-model validation.

Bound the Provider Comparison. Separate native inertia/bias operators from the shared contact law and update procedure. The spatial same-force geometry controls are postprocessing; the planar coincident-grip branch is a new continuation. A one-arm model needs explicit added contacts before it can answer two-hand questions.

Carry Forward the Existing Contact-Moment Qualification. Chapter 20 already documents the noncentral vector-damping force-pair moment under AffineDrift #4724 and UpstreamDrift #11195. Propagate the qualification to Chapter 17 without claiming a new discovery, a whole-system angular-momentum residual or the cause of the negative club moment. Chapter 16's central fibers are a distinct model.

Bound Human and Control Inferences. Nesbit/McGinnis use measured 3D markers mapped to a rigid planar club model; Miura combines measured illustrations and simplified models. Neither identifies a universally beneficial whole-body intervention. A failed model-controller experiment counts against the tested combination; separating causes requires evidence.

Contact Work and COM Work. An external force can change momentum without supplying energy at its contact. The revised chapter distinguishes local force power from the resultant-force COM kinetic-energy relation. Stationary sticking and prevented-rotation assumptions are explicit. The zero-gravity, supported two-mass example reconciles 20 J internal conversion, 20 J kinetic gain, 10 J COM gain and zero support work. A free-pair control preserves zero total momentum. The ground reaction enables the supported motion without becoming its energy source.

Gravity and Actuation Counted Once. A prescribed static external field admits an effective potential without adding Earth as a dynamical body. Gravity power and potential change are alternative ledger representations. An unpowered club has no internal actuator conversion: the golfer's input already enters through the hand interface. The same wrist work must not be added again under that club-only boundary.

Internal Power and Compatible Motion. Coincident positions alone do not guarantee cancellation. Pair power uses relative material-point velocities and relative angular velocities. Compatible ideal passive constraints give zero pairing; slip, storage, interface inertia and actuation require their own terms. A massless passive storage/loss balance is explicitly bounded to that model. A force perpendicular to relative motion still gives zero power.

Representation Versus Observer. Consistent rigid-point transport or axis relabeling preserves wrench power for the same observer. A nonrotating Galilean boost instead changes it by minus resultant force dotted with boost velocity. The pure-couple exception has zero resultant. Neither operation causes a physical change in the swing.

Resultant Wrench Versus Deformation. Rigid trajectory equivalence needs the same initial state, parameters, other loads and complete input history. A self-equilibrated axial load has zero resultant wrench but 2 W under the specified outward deformation field. Zero loads have the same resultant but zero power. This is a counterexample to unqualified flexible-body inference, not a measured effect size for grip or shaft deformation.

Recoil and Frame. Translational recoil follows the COM momentum identity for constant mass and total impulse over an interval. Large mass suppresses the quadratic term for bounded impulse, not the initial-velocity cross term. Local deformation, spin and support motion are separate. No infinite-Earth- mass limit at fixed gravitational constant and distance is used to justify a finite prescribed gravity field.

Explicit Body Inventories. Club, hands-plus-club, both complete upper limbs-plus-club and golfer-plus-club have named interfaces. Shoulder ports are external for the upper-limb inventory, while wrists and elbows are internal. Spanning muscles, tissues and contact elements still require an explicit model allocation. Enlarging the inventory does not uniquely identify muscle work or imply an isolated system.

Verification and Evidence. Energy closure does not independently prove anatomy, contact-law realism, angular-momentum closure or unique allocation. Pinned two-sided shaft-power and two-hand reconstruction accounts support the explanation within their reported scope. Human work estimates remain model dependent. The hypothetical transfer pathway requires compatible data, intervals and endpoint definitions.

Figure Semantics. The old combined gravity/ground arrow sat outside the outer Earth-inclusive boundary. The replacement classifies interactions and muscle conversion under three explicit body inventories. It makes no arrow imply positive energy transfer, and notes that effective field potential does not require including Earth. Only the existing `make_system_boundaries` function changes in the shared generator; four small private drawing helpers keep each changed function below 50 lines. All other existing function ASTs and top-level non-function nodes were checked unchanged. The helper extraction preserves the exact rendered RGBA pixels of the inspected figure.

**Distinct Evidence Questions.** Separate artifact identity, computational reproduction, independent verification and empirical validation. Define the chapter's reproduction/new-observation convention rather than treating terminology as universal. A repeated calculation can preserve a model error; two wrappers around shared dynamics are not independent physical validation.

**Comparison Contracts and Authenticity.** Raw hashes distinguish serializations even when decoded numbers agree; recomputing an erroneous result's checksum does not justify accepting it. The provider normalizes CRLF for named text suffixes and leaves binary bytes unchanged. Distinguish that contract from exact deployed-copy parity. A PDF magic header is not a cryptographic digital signature, and a bare digest does not authenticate authorship or science.

**Matched Observables and Uncertainty.** Specify body, point, observer, axes, units, event, interval and processing before comparing numbers. The 43 m/s versus 154.8 km/h example requires conversion. State nonnegative absolute and relative tolerances with correct dimensions, trajectory alignment and norm. Numerical error, measurement uncertainty and model discrepancy stay distinct.

**Reproduction Beyond Seeds.** Preserve sampled inputs and their case assignments, generator/call order, environment and execution evidence. A repeated seed with an extra draw assigns different samples. The binary64 1e16, 1, -1e16 example illustrates order sensitivity without claiming all parallel runs are nondeterministic. A listed command is not a completed run.

**Verification Without Physical Validation.** The unit-inertia oscillator at two natural frequencies conserves each model's own exact energy but predicts different angles. Explicit-midpoint step refinement converges to each declared model, including the wrong model for a specified target. Algebraic contact power, integrated energy residuals, numerical convergence and empirical adequacy answer different questions. Golf transfer arguments require matched boundaries, signed powers, storage/loss terms, events and uncertainty.

**Actual Validator and Publication Scope.** The pinned entry point invokes manifest, numerical-claim, claim-evidence, external-review and PDF-profile checks; it is not merely a hash checker. Listing presets prints commands without executing them. Pinned computational qualification does not establish archival accessibility; reported tagging/font failures and unresolved human, equipment, tissue, full-contact and external-deposit requirements remain. Source inspection here is not a fresh provider qualification run.

**Representable Limits and Figure Provenance.** Preserve valid unresolved scientific statuses while blocking promotion. Distinguish schema failures from untested hypotheses, measurements from synthetic outputs, and numerical plots from schematics. No fake dataset is required for the reviewer-path illustration. Correct its caption/alt text to the six actual boxes, removing the previously claimed reproduction-result box; the figure itself is retained.

**Revision and Preservation.** Replace mutable provider-main links with the already reviewed immutable revision. Separate source identity, long-term availability, URL reachability and deployed-copy parity. Convert unverified universal descriptions of site compliance into explicit maintenance goals. Failed runs and contradictory implementations remain part of the record.

**Net Joint Demand and Bounded Allocation.** Define signed musculotendon path derivatives, external-load accounting, and the separate passive-load convention. A force-map null space does not guarantee unlimited feasible allocations. The two-antagonist fixture has a bounded interval, with dynamic realizability as an additional condition; fully specified internal states can further constrain forces.

**Excitation, Force, and Power.** Distinguish the sampled electrical signal from activation state and force. Signed path power is 6 W for all feasible illustrated force pairs; it is neither individual fibre power nor metabolic expenditure. EMG alone cannot identify club power or eliminate unobserved force sources.

**Geometric Stiffness and Impedance.** Derive K = sum(k r^2 - F r-prime) for a declared local elastic model. Finite differences verify +1.8 versus -0.2 N m/rad with and without the geometric contribution, despite positive material stiffness. Distinguish local stiffness from a movement-curve slope and from full dynamic impedance. Do not infer whole-joint instability or universal co-contraction benefits.

**Elastic Energy and Transmission Timing.** Replace force storage with strain-energy storage; 50-to-100 N loading stores an additional 0.375 J in the stated linear example. Series stiffness does not itself define delay. Separate tendon slack length and short-range stiffness from the provider's phenomenological rotational dead zone; its zero-gap comparison bounds its claimed advantage.

**Anatomical Coordinates and Contact Loads.** Separate scapular/shoulder motion, forearm pronation, carpal wrist motion, contact moments and anatomical joint demand. Axis projection and work-conjugate generalized torque require the stated kinematic mapping. Coordinate recommendations and bone-tracking evidence do not identify a golf scapular driver.

**Study Attribution and Human Evidence.** Correct Kao/Pink/Jobe/Perry attribution. Preserve exact sample/measurement scope: 15 competitive men / four bilateral scapular muscles; 15 subelite right-handed men / bilateral ECU. Do not invent Kao electrode construction, interpret nonsignificance as equivalence, or claim identified force allocations.

**Full-Wrench Matching and Fixed Geometry.** Two synthetic bilateral allocations give the same 100 N resultant, 12 N m moment, and 236 W at a specified rigid twist. At fixed contact geometry, changing arm posture alone cannot change the common-force lever arm. Moving both contacts 2 cm relative to the same origin changes the moment to 14 N m unless other loads change. The provider's scalar control-induced angular-acceleration demand is weaker than full-wrench or full-trajectory matching.

**Discriminating Experiments and Presentation.** Match measurements to hypotheses; randomized cues do not randomize the adopted biological mediator. Preserve supported/contradicted/inconclusive/untested distinctions, practical uncertainty and participant holdout. Pin the provider references and bound the schematic as coupled anatomy rather than interchangeable independent actuators or measured pathways.

**Unilateral Cord Versus Bilateral Guide:** Tangent-only initial release velocity. For the top of a circular path ($2\text{ kg}$, $1\text{ m}$ radius), evaluation at speeds $1\text{ m/s}$ and $4\text{ m/s}$ yields upward reactions $\lambda = 17.62\text{ N}$ and $-12.38\text{ N}$. At the circle top, upward is outward: the positive value would require compression and is invalid for a cord, while the negative value corresponds to feasible inward tension. The original Flash draft reversed this conclusion; rejected by the lead against the numerical force balance.

**Constraint Formulation & Solvability:** Assumes symmetric positive-definite (SPD) mass, full row-rank constraint Jacobian $J$, and consistent kinematic initialization. Distinguishes physical generalized constraint forces $Q_c = J^T \lambda$ from arbitrary multiplier normalizations, and isolates fixed bilateral constraint modes from contact impact events.

**Constraint Power & Work:** Ideal bilateral constraints do zero virtual work, but moving prescribed constraints can do actual physical work: $P_c = -\lambda \cdot \phi_t$. In the moving constraint example ($2\text{ kg}$, $x = \alpha t^2$, $\alpha = 1\text{ m/s}^2$, evaluated at one second), an applied force of $3\text{ N}$ plus a reaction force of $1\text{ N}$ yields a kinetic-energy-rate balance of $6\text{ W} + 2\text{ W} = 8\text{ W}$.

**Indeterminacy & Net-Wrench Observations:** Differentiates unique, fully specified forward constraint reactions from redundant Jacobian rows and incomplete net-wrench observations. For duplicate rows $[1, 0]$ and $[2, 0]$, non-unique multipliers such as $\lambda = [-2, 0]^T$ or $[-0.4, -0.8]^T$ produce the identical generalized constraint force $Q_c = [-2, 0]^T$.

**Two-Hand Couple Mechanics:** Equal and opposite force increments applied by two hands cancel net linear force but can generate a club moment couple $\Delta M = (r_L - r_R) \times f$. An axial null offset contrasts with a $0.2\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ transverse couple at $0.2\text{ m}$ separation; this mechanical balance carries no automatic claim of biological feasibility.

**Kinematic Drift & Club Power:** Retains one drift term across four input cases ($y_{PD} = y_P + y_D - y_0$), accounts for endpoint kinematic $\dot{J}$ contributions, and restricts claims to the forward policy/history scope. A purely radial club force that generates zero moment about the center of mass (COM) does not imply zero instantaneous power at the point of application.

**Compliance Versus Constraint Limits:** Mechanical stiffness is distinguished from time delay and rigid-body force convergence. For an undamped $1\text{ kg}$ system with initial displacement $F_0 / k$, with $F_0 = 1\text{ N}$, the force amplitude remains $1\text{ N}$ while displacement and stored strain energy vanish as $k \to \infty$. Analysis maintains strict separation between ideal algebraic reactions, elastic potential storage, and viscous damping.

**Empirical Grounding & Presentation:** Enforces hypothesis-specific falsification, states explicit computational provider and human subject boundaries, ensures clear legibility for circular trajectory figures, and prunes redundant cautionary prose.

**Registration Scope:** A timestamped analysis plan makes changes auditable; it cannot prevent amendments or guarantee sound inference. Preserve original plans, dated amendments, outcome-access state, predeclared contingencies, exploratory analyses and unfavorable outcomes. An inspected pilot is not untouched confirmation. Protocol completeness alone does not qualify an instrument or study.

**Measurement and Identifiability:** Calibrated wrenches, reconstructed power, stiffness, muscle force and model counterfactuals have different observational requirements. A split-grip transducer does not directly measure every individual hand-wrench component. Timing uncertainty includes clock offset/drift, latency, resampling and event localization; covariance assumptions matter. Provider sampling rates and tolerances are protocol-specific. Preserve trial dispositions and differential quality failures; missing data are not measured zeros.

**Filtering and Closure:** Even two zero-phase filters can attenuate a shared signal differently. In the constant-mass illustration, residual r = H_F F - m H_a a = m(H_F-H_a)a. Matching the linear filters closes this particular example, not arbitrary nonlinear multibody dynamics. The periodic test excludes finite-record boundary effects; the prose separately explains acausal event/edge contamination. Sidestep and landing studies do not establish a universal golf cutoff.

**Control and Null Boundaries:** Frame/reference invariance, physical interventions and deliberately corrupted channels test different propositions. For opposite forces, M = (r_L-r_R) cross f + C_L + C_R. Zero separation removes only the separated-force couple; coincident hands with direct z-moment projections -0.3 and -0.2 N·m retain -0.5 N·m. Human geometry changes can change force/control as well. Temporal surrogates and label permutations must respect dependence and the actual randomization.

**Causal Mediation:** Randomizing an instruction does not randomize a measured mediator. With independent centered unit-variance T, U and E, M=T+U+E and Y=U yield a naive regression product 1 times 1/2 despite zero structural effect through M. U is a pretreatment common cause; E is independent variation in M, not a separate observation-error model. Adjustment for observed U removes this association in the toy. Hierarchical modeling alone does not identify mediation. A failed manipulation check does not erase an instruction's possible total effect through other pathways.

**Participant Inference:** Separate prediction for new golfers from later swings of known golfers, and prescribed baseline calibration from test-outcome leakage. For a balanced random-intercept grand mean, variance is sigma_u^2/n + sigma_e^2/(nm). Twelve people, ten swings each, between-person variance 4 and within-person variance 1 give 0.3417 versus a naive 0.0417, ratio 8.2. This is not a universal design effect for paired contrasts, where stable intercepts may cancel. Plan the actual estimand, covariance, missingness and multiplicity.

**Decision Regions:** Nonsignificance is not equivalence. In the idealized normal known-standard-error example, estimate zero with s=0.2 N·m gives a 90% interval approximately [-0.329,0.329] within illustrative bounds +/-0.5 N·m; s=0.5 gives approximately [-0.822,0.822], inconclusive. The interval corresponds to alpha=.05 TOST under the stated model, not a universal interval level, golf threshold, exact-zero finding or exemption from multiplicity/cluster inference.

**Evidence and Readiness:** Distinguish bounded support, contradiction, inconclusive results and unexecuted tests; update the figure accordingly. A synthetic intake dry run and computational qualification do not establish human evidence or laboratory readiness. The pinned provider's missing governed full-contract dataset does not mean no relevant study exists anywhere. State staged testing, consent/data authority, model fitting versus prediction and hypotheses with outcomes that remain open.

**Model Families and Figure Meaning.** The earlier caption described models while its actual graphic ranked equation identity through replicated outcomes. Replace that mismatch with six model families connected through an explicit comparison contract. A flexible shaft, moving base, spatial contact and biological allocation are branches with capability memberships, not guaranteed nested additions or a monotonic confidence ranking. Mark the family descriptions as modeling questions rather than claims of execution.

**Available Outputs and Compatible Power.** Define each model's output map on full state, input and parameters, including units, frame, reference, port, event and error scope. Unsupported quantities remain unavailable, not measured zeros. A resultant wrench paired with one rigid twist only captures compatible rigid motion. Two outward 10 N endpoint forces with outward 0.2 m/s endpoint velocities give 4 W external input despite zero resultant force and moment. The example illustrates deformation power omitted by rigid reduction; it does not claim that all input instantly becomes stored strain energy.

**Full State and Intervention Identity.** Equal reduced motion can hide elastic or activation state. In a two-mass spring fixture with displacements from equilibrium, k=100 N/m and observed mass1=1 kg, z=q2-q1=±0.01 m gives a1=±1 m/s² while q1=v1=0 initially. The unobserved mass2=2 kg has opposite momentum-rate contribution, preserving total linear momentum. Keep prescribed inverse comparisons, dynamic forward evolution, instantaneous command deletion and altered input histories distinct; register lifts and initial energy.

**Complexity and Identifiability.** Added state does not universally increase all uncertainty or destroy identifiability. Separate approximation bias, numerical error, parameter uncertainty and ambiguous internal variables. Data, known parameters and justified constitutive restrictions determine whether additional structure is informative. Training fit and anatomical appearance alone do not establish predictive improvement.

**The Independent Part of an Implementation.** Pin the reviewed upstream source. Its common-state MuJoCo/Lagrange--Christoffel comparison is distinct from its reduced forward MuJoCo/Pinocchio comparison. The latter uses native inertia-and-bias operators but shared projected compliance and a shared semi-implicit state update. This is bounded operator transport, not independent native contact-solver or integrator parity. Compare physical reactions with matched coordinates and boundary laws; redundant multipliers need not match. Package capabilities are not executed project evidence.

**Failure Status and Capability Scope.** Failed closure prevents numerical qualification; a resolved falsifier may contradict a registered prediction; insufficient information is inconclusive; unrun comparisons are untested. Changed assumptions can reverse a conditional result without refuting mechanics. The pinned finite-base study reports 576 numerical passes but zero eligible total-work-matched comparison cells, which supplies no delivery-benefit estimate. Articulated short-horizon successes do not imply unrestricted anatomical transport; completed documentation does not imply completed experiments.

**Ensemble Fractions and Statistical Inference.** A chosen 95% sign rule is conditional on scenario design and weights. Identical outcomes produce 75% with equal weights and 30% with weights (0.1,0.1,0.1,0.7). For 95/100 independent Bernoulli successes, SciPy's independent Wilson calculation gives [0.888249530768,0.978456320846] at approximate 95% confidence. It is not an exact-coverage guarantee, a population lower bound of 0.95, or a justified interval for an arbitrary correlated grid.

**Measurements and Published Golf Evidence.** Instrument selection follows the estimand and alternatives; EMG is not direct muscle force. The absence of a qualifying governed deposit in the pinned project is not global absence of golf measurements. McNally/McPhee 2018 provides a six-DOF carry-distance optimization example with constrained timing, candidate center-face impacts, a torso-before-pelvis solution and grip-kinematic discrepancies. Those limits illustrate conditional model evaluation; neither visual resemblance nor the optimized torque generators identify human muscle control.

**Coordinate-Compatible Loads and Power.** Declare both link angles absolute and the wrist angle relative. An internal wrist actuator exerts equal-and-opposite couples, so the absolute-coordinate load is (tau_s-tau_w,tau_w), whereas the relative-coordinate load is (tau_s,tau_w). Transform the inertia and bias consistently through theta=Aq. The manufactured rates (2,5) rad/s and actuator torques (3,4) N m give 18 W, not the naive 26 W. Numerical checks independently verify power, kinetic energy and acceleration equivalence; the omitted arm-side wrist contribution is -8 W.

**Configuration-Dependent Coupling.** Give the physically parameterized absolute-coordinate inertia and velocity bias, including transported distal mass. Set delta=theta1-theta2=-phi explicitly. At delta=+pi/2, inertia coefficients (2,1,1) and absolute rates (2,0) produce distal acceleration 4 rad/s² without gravity or actuation despite an instantaneous diagonal inertia. A second nonzero-rate fixture verifies cancellation of the inertial work term and the mass-matrix derivative term. Deleting one off-diagonal entry without the associated energy and force structure is not physical decoupling.

**Transport, Relative Motion and Energy.** Distinguish absolute club rotation from relative wrist rotation and vector clubhead velocity from an invalid scalar speed sum. Carrying can change distal motion before rapid relative release, but energy gain requires the work balance. Rigid-link mechanical storage is kinetic and gravitational potential energy; shaft strain requires deformation state. Internal exchanges redistribute energy, while boundary work changes its total. A geometric sketch supplies no measured velocities, forces or energy history.

**Moving-Hand Reactions and Contact Power.** Both force components applied at the hand have zero moment about that hand, although a transverse force can have a moment about the club COM. For a body-fixed hand point, include m r_G/H cross a_H in the planar angular balance. The manufactured m=2 kg, I_G=0.5 kg m², r=(1,0) m and a_H=(0,1) m/s² state has angular acceleration -0.8 rad/s² and hand force (0,0.4) N without a couple. Its COM moment is -0.4 N m and its power at hand velocity (0,3) m/s is 1.2 W. The test reconciles COM and hand-reference balances and kinetic-energy rate. Club-side couple power uses absolute club rate; whole-system wrist-actuator power uses the relative rate.

**Singular Limits and Locking Events.** A vanishing distal inertia does not universally remove reactions: with mass and COM inertia proportional to epsilon, unit offset and finite unit couple, angular acceleration is 1/(2epsilon) and tangential hand force stays 0.5 N. The support reaction couple also persists. Bounded-acceleration families behave differently; the singular endpoint requires a reduced model. Zero length need not remove rotary inertia. Distinguish an already locked wrist from imposing an inelastic lock. For diagonal generalized inertia (2,1), rates (1,0), wrist constraint and no other generalized impulse, projection gives (2/3,2/3) and kinetic energy falls from 1 to 2/3. Smooth conservative energy checks do not forbid physically dissipative events or gravity/preload-driven motion from rest.

**Actuator Rank and Intervention Meaning.** Zero command is an input value, not a change in the rank of available actuator directions. Separate actuator command from net torque even for a single pendulum. A copied-state acceleration comparison differs from an integrated branch whose state subsequently diverges. Setting velocities to zero removes all velocity-dependent effects present, including damping when modeled; it does not isolate inertial coupling by definition. Preserve joint modes and internal actuator or elastic state where relevant.

**Conditional Timing and Evidence.** Torque timing comparisons depend on work, rise time, initial state and the output event; peak speed anywhere is not impact speed. Sharp's three-link optimization supports a conditional timing result, with net wrist torque distinct from parameterized actuator input and limit-stop reactions. Putnam's kicking/throwing synthesis is not a golf intervention study. Neither fitted kinematics nor manufactured checks identify human muscle strategy. Added relevant physics can reverse an intervention's benefit without violating mechanics; accounting identities survive extensions, while timing and sign claims require retesting.

**Figure Geometry and Scope.** The old three panels retained the same relative angle despite a carry/reorient/handoff narrative and cropped distal endpoints. Change the relative angles to -1.6, -0.8 and -0.1 radians, show both complete connected links, and derive common bounds from all endpoints. Label the panels Folded, Opening and Nearly Aligned and explicitly identify illustrative geometry rather than a simulated trajectory. Retain the asset path for compatibility. The test verifies endpoint containment and changing relative geometry; only make_carry_release changes in the shared generator.
